subject: Performance SLO & Private VPC qualification — Acme (post-call follow-up)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@acme.com>, Emily Cho <emily.cho@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-02-12T15:20:00-08:00
Subject: Performance SLO & Private VPC qualification — Acme (post-call follow-up)

Hi Sanjay / Emily —

Thanks again for the sync today. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment on the performance and networking requirements for a Private/VPC deployment: 

Summary / requirements we captured:
- Target latency: p95 <= 120ms for single-request streaming responses; p50 target 40-60ms for non-streaming inference.
- Throughput: baseline 50 rps sustained, expected peak 250 rps during batch jobs; concurrency target ~500 active user sessions.
- Streaming: client-side streaming for long-form generation (~5-10s responses) required; need to support chunked/resume behavior.
- KV/cache sizing: anticipated model KV cache increase given average prompt length ~1.2k tokens.
- Reliability: failover to hosted fallback if private capacity is constrained.

Network/Private deployment specifics we need from your side:
1) Preferred connectivity: VPN vs cloud-peering (Do you prefer IPSec VPN or direct VPC Peering?)
2) Egress constraints: are there NAT/firewall rules that block outbound connections or require proxy?
3) Internal latency budgets: what is your internal app-to-model budget (ms) for edge->app->model hop?
4) Expected IPs/CIDR we can peer to and any allowed ports (443, 50051 for gRPC, 22 for jump hosts if needed)
5) Any corporate proxy/inspect rules that would affect TLS or streaming chunking

Attachments: I attached our SLO matrix and a short network checklist that maps what our deployment team typically needs (slo-matrix.pdf, network-checklist.xlsx).

Next steps: 
- Sanjay / Emily to share network topology and whether they prefer VPN or peering (ideally by EOD 2028-02-13).
- Redwood to run a quick network qualification and propose a network workshop with your infra team (we suggest 60-90 minutes).
- Dev team (cc'ed) will propose preliminary config for throughput/concurrency based on your answers.

If that looks right I can schedule the workshop — would Thursday morning PT or Friday afternoon PT work for your network folks?

Thanks,

Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
(jordan.blake@redwood.ai)
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@acme.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Cho <emily.cho@acme.com>, network-team@acme.com
Date: 2028-02-13T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO & Private VPC qualification — Acme (post-call follow-up)

Thanks Jordan — good notes, appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers inline.

On 2028-02-12, Jordan Blake wrote:
> - Target latency: p95 <= 120ms for single-request streaming responses; p50 target 40-60ms for non-streaming inference.

We can accept p95 <= 150ms across the internal app->model hop; our goal is 120ms but want to set realistic expectations while we validate network path.

> - Throughput: baseline 50 rps sustained, expected peak 250 rps during batch jobs; concurrency target ~500 active user sessions.

Confirmed. Our infra owners expect these numbers during initial rollout. We'll provide time-of-day distribution.

> Network/Private deployment specifics we need from your side:
> 1) Preferred connectivity: VPN vs cloud-peering

We prefer IPSec VPN to start (we have approvals already), with peering as a follow-up option.

> 2) Egress constraints

We do egress via an outbound proxy that does TLS termination for inspection. We will check whether streaming chunking is allowed through the proxy; our security team (network-team@acme.com) is looped.

> 3) Internal latency budgets

App-to-model budget for UI-critical flows: 200ms; background jobs allow up to 500ms.

> Attachments: I attached our SLO matrix and a short network checklist

Attaching our initial network trace from the test we ran this morning (network-trace-2028-02-12.zip) and a short topology diagram.

Next steps from our side: we'll confirm proxy behavior by EOD 2028-02-13 and set up time for the network workshop.

— Sanjay
Sanjay Patel
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Corp
(sanjay.patel@acme.com)
Attachment: network-trace-2028-02-12.zip
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-02-13T11:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO & Private VPC qualification — Acme (post-call follow-up)

Thanks Sanjay — good to see the trace. A few clarifying technical questions from the deployment side: 

1) VPN: if IPSec, do you have a vendor/router model and a preferred cipher set? We typically validate MTU changes for streaming.
2) Proxy TLS termination: does the proxy re-encrypt upstream (true TLS passthrough) or terminate and re-TLS? If it terminates and re-TLSs, we need to confirm HTTP/2 and gRPC passthrough behavior for streaming.
3) Ports: we will propose 443 (HTTPS) and 50051 (gRPC) as required; confirm any proxies altering SNI.
4) Busy-hour profile: can you share a 1-week sample with 5-min granularity for peak planning?

Action: I can run a lightweight synthetic test (mTLS-enabled if you prefer) from our staging instance to your VPN endpoint once the team provides VPN gateway IP/CIDR and a test cert. That will give us a first-party baseline for p50/p95 and packet reassembly behavior.

I'll also prepare an initial capacity sketch (instances and expected GPU config) aligned to 50rps baseline / 250rps peak and will include recommendations on batching and KV cache sizing.

Available slots for the network workshop: 2028-02-15 10:00-11:30 PT or 2028-02-16 13:00-14:30 PT. Which works best?

— Dev Patel
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
(dev.patel@redwood.ai)
